## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cakkhuviññāṇādipañha* ("The Question on the Process of Visual Cognition") is a dialogue in the *Milindapañha* [SuttaCentral]. It examines psychological and cognitive processes, specifically the nature and occurrence of visual cognition (*cakkhuviññāṇa*) and mental cognition [SuttaCentral]. Modern English translations of the text include one by John Kelly [SuttaCentral].
In the Chinese Buddhist canon, the text has a direct parallel in the *Nagasena Bhikṣu Sūtra*, preserved at T 1670b 2.29 under the title "Visual-consciousness and Mental-consciousness" [SuttaCentral]. Automatic text analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across Abhidhamma and Nikāya texts, sharing significant material with the *Uppādavāra* of the *Yamaka* (Ya 3.2.1 and Ya 10.2.1), the *Ñāṇavibhaṅga* of the *Vibhaṅga* (Vb 16), the *Anantarapaccayakathā* (Kv 14.3) and *Sābhogātikathā* (Kv 10.5) of the *Kathāvatthu*, the *Mahātaṇhāsaṅkhaya Sutta* (MN 38), and neighbouring questions in the *Milindapañha* such as the *Phassalakkhaṇapañha* (Mil 3.3.8) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus records cross-language computational alignments with the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) and the Tibetan translation of the *Yogācārabhūmiviniścayasaṃgrahaṇī* (D 4038) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
